links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM assessments across two repeated runs (consistent assessment rate, Cohen's kappa)
links.effect: Larger models showed high repeatability (Cohen's κ up to 0.99); smaller models like Qwen3-8B declined (κ = 0.69). Domain consistency was lower for disease burden.
links.quote: Larger parameter scales LLMs demonstrated higher accuracy and repeatability, with Cohen’s κ up to 0.99, whereas smaller LLMs like Qwen3-8B showed marked declines (κ = 0.69).

unlisted_practices: Expert-developed structured prompts with prompt engineering for nutrition risk screening
Comparing LLMs of different parameter scales and openness on accuracy, consistency and processing time

screen.reason: The study conducts an offline retrospective benchmark of 8 LLMs using real-world inpatient EHRs to automate nutrition risk screening (NRS-2002). It does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard comparison.
